    Keep Claude Code’s prompt cache warm during breaks and show the estimated cost before a cold send.

    🪝 Claude Code hooks + an installable plugin marketplace: safety, cost, observability, productivity.
  • itr-wala 886 129
    File your Indian income tax return (ITR) from your terminal. Deterministic tax engine, both regimes, AY 2026-27. Claude Code / Codex / Gemini skill.
  • reddit-mcp-buddy 894 110
    Clean, LLM-optimized Reddit MCP server. Browse posts, search content, analyze users. No fluff, just Reddit data.
  • algo-sensei 302 64
    Your AI-powered LeetCode & DSA mentor for Claude Code and Claude.ai. Master algorithms through intelligent guidance, progressive hints, and pattern recognition training—not just copy-pasting solutions. Features: Mock interviews, code review, multi-language support (Python, Java, C++, JS, Go). Learn to think like a senior engineer. 🥋

Karan Bansal

I build open-source tools for AI coding agents and write about what I learn from building and using AI systems.

Start here

  • Understand AI: AI Dojo has free explainers and exercises on how AI systems work, where they help, and where they fall short.
  • Use Claude Code tooling: Claude Code Hooks provides installable hooks for secret protection, Git safety, cost visibility, and observability. These are guardrails, not a sandbox. Selected as a tool demo for Black Hat Europe 2026 Arsenal.
  • Understand cache costs: Cache Tax estimates the rewrite cost before a cold send and can keep selected sessions warm during breaks. Warming costs tokens; estimates use API-equivalent prices, not extra subscription charges.
  • Compare mods: Awesome Claude Code Mods is a catalogue of community mods, with scan results showing what each one can access. The scan is a static check of the source, not a safety rating.
  • File an Indian tax return: itr-wala is a skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini that prepares an Indian income tax return from your terminal. Tested code does the tax math, not the model. You pay, submit, and e-verify yourself, and it is not professional tax advice.
  • Read Reddit from an AI assistant: Reddit MCP Buddy is an MCP server for browsing and searching Reddit. It works only with Reddit API credentials that Reddit has already approved; Reddit no longer accepts new requests.
  • Read or watch: Writing and talks on AI systems, coding agents, and agent security.

I am an open-source systems engineer who turns ambiguous, cross-layer failures into shipped, reviewable fixes. I build developer tooling and coding-agent infrastructure, and I operate production systems where correctness, recovery, and observability are not optional.

My public work spans compiler/runtime behavior, Kubernetes policy validation, CLI execution safety, atomic storage, cloud integrations, package resolution, authentication, performance measurement, CI, and deployment reliability.

I enter unfamiliar systems, find the real failure boundary, build the regression proof, and stay with the change until it is useful upstream.

Products I maintain

opencode-multi-auth-codex

A reliability layer for Codex OAuth in OpenCode: account routing, session controls, dashboard, and operational tooling.

opencode-tps-meter

Makes coding-agent throughput observable with live streaming and final output-token measurements in the OpenCode TUI.

opencode-status-signals

Turns hidden agent state into immediate visual feedback through OpenCode's native theme system.

Proof of work

What I bring to a difficult codebase

  • Deep debugging across runtime, API, storage, infrastructure, and deployment boundaries
  • Regression tests and compatibility guards that make risky fixes maintainable
  • Production ownership: observability, safe migrations, CI, recovery, and release discipline
  • Maintainer-grade follow-through from unclear issue to reviewed, shipped result

Hi there!

I'm Oleksii, a senior software engineer at Uber, building software since 2007, and a lifelong learner. What I enjoy most is taking a complex technical idea, digging into it until it feels simple, and then distilling it into something minimal, visual, and interactive that makes it click for others too.

That's the thread running through most of my open-source 🚀 projects: algorithms and data structures in JavaScript, machine learning built from scratch, a neural network in a handful of functions, a self-parking car that learns through a genetic algorithm, and more.

I also write 📝 articles about learning, life, web development, and machine learning. My work has been featured in Hacker News, TechCrunch, JavaScript Weekly, Wikipedia, and MDN (publications).
